By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 88794 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. The Big Game has become a full menu of prop markets that attract both casual fans and seasoned bettors. From the opening coin toss to the l ength of the national anthem , and even the color of the post-game Gatorade shower , novelty wagers have become a major part of the experience and consistently draw heavy interest leading up to kickoff. Below, we break down some of the most popular Super Bowl props along with how they've performed historically, also providing some of our expert's predictions on whether the Seattle Seahawks or New England Patriots will lift the Lombardi Trophy. All odds below were taken from FanDuel Sportsbook as of Feb. 7. Expert Predictions Will Hill : Seahawks 27, Patriots 17 The Patriots have had a remarkable turnaround post-Bill Belichick, but the Seahawks will pose a significant step-up in competition compared to what the AFC bracket presented. I expect a low-scoring game, but I think the more talented Seahawks will ultimately pull away and win 27-17, with Sam Darnold taking home MVP. Chris Fallica : Seahawks 27, Patriots 23 I hate the game from a spread standpoint. It seems like a simple handicap where Seattle is better at every position group, and groupthink has the Seahawks winning comfortably. If anything, I’ll see if I can get a cheap Seahawks moneyline on the game, but I’m not going to lay 4.5 here. Sammy P : Seahawks 23, Patriots 20 After a low-scoring first quarter, I expect things to stay competitive the rest of the way. New England (15-5 ATS) made bettors money all season long and that mostly came in the favorite role. Mike Vrabel is a tremendous underdog coach and that song should remain the same this Sunday in Santa Clara. Geoff Schwartz : Seahawks 24, Patriots 13 I have the game 24-13 for the Seahawks. The Seahawks have been the best team wire-to-wire this season and the best case for the Patriots in this game is Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold turning back into a pumpkin, which I don't expect. He's been nails this postseason. The Seattle defense is going to sit in zone coverage and force New England to work for all its yards, which is difficult without dynamic playmakers at the skill positions. The Seahawks win this game comfortably. National Anthem For years, sports fans have bet on the length of the Star Spangled Banner, among other anthem-related props. NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game. The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover. Sign me up. The Chiefs' offense has been playing its best football in years over the last month. I understand the competition hasn't been great, but great teams should beat the heck out of bad defenses. Kansas City finally has a wide receiver corps good enough for a complete passing game. The Chiefs might also have the best running back duo in the NFL, which will continue to matter as Kenneth Walker III works through a lower-leg injury. I do worry about the Chiefs' offensive line against the Bills' defensive line. That's an advantage for Buffalo, but I trust Mahomes and Andy Reid to have a plan to navigate it. It feels like the Chiefs hold some things back against the Bills, knowing they'll likely see them again in the postseason. But this is the best the Chiefs have played entering a Bills game in years, and I believe they want to win this one. They're also starting a brutal stretch of games that will define their season, and they need to start it with a win. highlights: Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites).

The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career.

If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.

By Vaughn Dalzell , By Vaughn Dalzell Published November 22, 2026 10:05 AM Add on Google Facebook Twitter Email Add on Google After a hot 4-1 Thursday Night, let’s have a winning Sunday! Here are my eight best bets for the day. Best of luck! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Titans at Cowboys (-7.5): O/U 54.5 The Titans and Cowboys meet in a battle of two of the worst defenses in the NFL. The Titans are 4-0 to the Over in the last four games, while the Cowboys are 3-1 to the Over in that same span. Dallas is 7-3 to the Over on the year, and Tennessee is 6-3, both ranking top five. The Titans and Cowboys have allowed opponents to score on 46% of drives, ranking 30th and 31st, and both allow a passing success rate of 50% or higher, ranking 29th and 31st — you get the drift. Totals of 54 or higher in the last three seasons are 14-4 to the Over. This one has the making of at least one team reaching 30 points. I like the Over 54.5 up to 55.5. Lean Tennessee +7.5 as they’ve drawn sharp money. Pick: Over 54.5 (1 unit) Jared Goff O/U 32.5 Pass Attempts vs Buccaneers Now that Baker Mayfield is in, we are back on Jared Goff’s passing attempts over 32.5. He would have likely cashed the over 34.5 last week against New England, but Drake Maye’s injury threw off the entire game flow. With Mayfield in, plus the Buccaneers defense being capable of offering resistance in the rush game, this is a good spot for Goff to go over after under his passing attempts in five-straight games. The Bucs run the eighth-most zone coverage at 79.2%, and Goff ranks top 10 in completion percentage (71%), passer rating (100.8), and catchable rate (76.9%) against zone coverage. I’d go up to 33.5. Pick: Jared Goff Over 32.5 Pass Attempts (1.5 units) Patrick Mahomes O/U 30.5 Pass Attempts vs Cardinals Much like Matthew Stafford and the Rams last week, I don’t expect many passes to be thrown in the second half on the Chiefs side. Stafford threw three passes in the third quarter and none in the fourth as the Rams waxed the Cardinals 34-6. With a spread of -15.5, it’s safe to say the Chiefs should be in a positive game script, meaning most of Patrick Mahomes ’ damage will come in the first half. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and a season-high five touchdowns against Atlanta on 22-of-35 (62.9%). The Chiefs’ offense is pretty depleted, and despite not having Kenneth Walker , Emmett Johnson proved he can handle the bulk of the ground work. I like Mahomes to go under 30.5 pass attempts to 29.5. This opened at 31.5. Pick: Patrick Mahomes Under 30.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Saquon Barkley O/U 55.5 Rushing Yards vs Steelers Steelers versus Eagles smells like an Under and an offensive struggle. Saquon Barkley ’s props have moved on the move downward over the last few days. This situation is similar to Jonathan Taylo r and the Colts; much like Taylor, Barkley’s snap share and usage will continue to decline as the Eagles lose more games and save him for next season. Barkley had a 58% snap share last week, marking the third time he’s crossed 50%. It won’t happen that often the rest of the season. With less snaps equals less opportunities. The best bet is fading Saquon every week, and I have to lean toward fading the Eagles until they start covering. At 1-8 ATS and 7 straight outright losses. Maybe the bye week helped them, but I doubt it. Pick: Saquon Barkley Under 55.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Saints at Bears (-11.5): O/U 48.5 Chicago coming out of a bye week is certainly an appealing bet-on team. The offense has been cooking with 31, 30, 34, and 27 points since Caleb Williams returned. Those games came against some pretty good defenses too: the Falcons, Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers. The Saints have only allowed three teams to reach 30 points on them: the Lions, Raiders, and Falcons. Better yet, the Saints have played some mediocre passing attacks in the last four games: Bryce Young , Shedeur Sanders , Aaron Rodgers , and Jameis Winston . I don’t think that group has prepared the Saints’ defense for what they’re about to face. The last factor: the Saints are 3-0 ATS on the road this year, but two of those road games came in Weeks 1-2, and the other on October 18 (Week 6). The Saints have either been at home or in Paris in seven of the past eight games. This will be a tough road contest, and if you fall behind early, I don’t think New Orleans could dig themselves out, so I like Chicago -11.5, but love the team total over 29.5 up to 30.5. Pick: Bears Team Total Over 29.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Cam Skattebo O/U 54.5 Rushing Yards vs. Jaguars Cam Skattebo has one of the trap lines of the week. Skattebo recorded 58 or more in six out of seven games he’s received a carry, and posted 124 and 78 in the last two games. This is one of those stinker lines in general; only if the Giants can keep this within a two-possession game could Skattebo hit the over. The Jaguars have a tendency to make teams abandon the run when they start to fall behind. Similar to Tony Pollard with the Titans last week, he was on a mini-monster run, and they were hanging a line that he crushed all season, but went way under versus the Jaguars with nine carries and 33 yards. Pollard had eight receptions on nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. I think the Giants’ backs will be important to the pass game because it’s going to be hard to avoid obvious passing or rushing situations. I like Skattebo to go under 54.5 rushing yards, down to 51.5. Pick: Cam Skattebo Under 54.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Raiders at Broncos (-10.5): O/U 40.5 I was most impressed with that Vegas opening drive last week, getting Fernando Mendoza comfortable and using his famous Indiana draw play to get his first NFL touchdown, of course, without the twisting and contorting. This week, I would look for a slow start and a lack of points from the Raiders offense, especially after the Brock Bowers injury. Bowers barely practiced on Thursday and is fighting to play, but if he is out, I don’t know if anyone saw the second half last week. The Raiders had -2 yards of offense on 3 drives in the second quarter, and -15 yards on the first two drives of the fourth quarter before moving the ball down the field for a field goal to lose by eight. It was horrible. Denver is a top-six first-quarter and first-half defense in PPG at 2.7 and 8.8. I could only look at either backing the Broncos on the first-quarter or first-half spreads, or taking the Under on the Raiders 1Q and 1H Team Totals. I will start with the Broncos first quarter -2.5. Denver has scored in five of the last six first quarters, and Las Vegas has trailed in three of five first quarters on the road — the two they didn’t were against the Jets (led 7-6) and Chargers (tied 0-0). Pick: Broncos 1Q -2.5 (1 unit) Vikings vs 49ers (-3.5): O/U 46.5 Brock Purdy goes from playing Dallas, which is one of the worst defenses in the NFL, to playing Minnesota in Mexico City. The Vikings have one of the best defenses in the NFL, and the altitude and location could throw these teams off a bit, specifically San Francisco. Mike Evans is questionable, and if he’s out, I really like the Under 46.5 in this matchup. The 49ers have hit the over game total five times this season against the Cowboys, Raiders, Cardinals, Dolphins, and Seahawks. Four of those make a ton of sense. The Vikings wouldn’t. The Vikings are an NFL-best 8-1 to the Under, 5-0 to the Under as an underdog, and 5-0 to the Under in non-division games.
